slides.title: Copy. Paste. Swap the *[brackets]*.
slides.body: Every prompt has [brackets]. Swap them for your real details: your business, your customer, your numbers. Paste into Claude. The more real detail you give, the more it sounds like you. Read every draft before you send it.

cards.p: Write a friendly reminder for invoice [number], [amount], due [date], to [client]. Two short sentences, assume they forgot, add my payment link [link]. No guilt, no threats.
Invoice [number] is [X] days late and my first reminder got no reply. Write a firm but kind follow up with a clear pay by date. Keep the relationship.
Turn these job notes into invoice lines: [paste]. One line per item in plain words, quantity and price in a table, total at the bottom. Flag anything I forgot to charge for.
Write a short deposit policy for my [business]: [percent] up front, when it is due, what happens if they cancel. Plain words a customer reads in 20 seconds.
I am raising [service] from [old price] to [new price] on [date]. Write a short note to current customers: one honest reason, the date, a thank you. No apologizing.
Write payment terms for my quotes in 4 bullets: when payment is due, how to pay, what counts as late, who to contact. Business: [type]. Friendly, no legal jargon.
Here are the questions customers ask me most: [paste]. Answer each in my voice in under 40 words, and end each with one clear next step.
A customer wants a refund: [situation]. My policy: [policy]. Write a calm, fair reply that says what I can do and keeps the door open. Under 100 words.
Reply to this complaint: [paste]. Own what went wrong in one sentence, say exactly how I will fix it and by when. No excuses, no groveling.
Write a text moving [customer] from [day] to [option 1] or [option 2]. Apologize once, give the reason in a few words, let them reply 1 or 2.
Write an after hours auto reply for my [business]: when I will answer, my booking link [link] for anyone ready, one line for urgent issues. Under 50 words.
Write a welcome text for new customers of my [business]: thank them, what happens next, what to prepare, how to reach me. Warm, under 60 words.
Here is a lead's message: [paste]. Is it worth a call? Give me the first question to ask, and the answer that would mean it is not a fit.
Write 3 texts to follow up a quote I sent [X] days ago for [job]. Text 1 checks in, text 2 adds something useful, text 3 closes the loop. Never desperate.
A customer says [service] is too expensive. Give me 3 replies that hold my price: one shows the value, one offers a smaller option, one lets them go politely.
Turn these notes into a one page proposal: [paste]. The problem, what I will do, the timeline, 3 price tiers, and one clear pick. Short sentences.
Customers usually buy [service]. Suggest 3 add ons that genuinely help them, and a one line way to offer each without sounding pushy.
Write a short text to customers who have not booked in [X] months. Remind them what I do, mention [season], make booking one tap: [link]. No discount.
Give me 30 post ideas for my [business] in [city]. Tie each one to a real question a customer asks. No generic tips.
Turn this 5 star review into 3 posts: [paste]. One story, one lesson, one before and after. Ask me before you use the customer's name.
Rewrite this headline 10 ways: [paste]. Specific and concrete, no clever wordplay. Mark the 2 you would test first and say why.
Write 3 slow season offers for my [business] that fill [month] without cheapening the brand. Add a one line pitch for each.
Write my Google Business Profile description for [business] in [area]: what I do, who for, why choose me. Plain words, under 750 characters.
Write a monthly email for my customers: one useful tip on [topic], one update, one clear way to book. Under 150 words. Match my voice: [sample].
Write a 2 sentence text asking [name] for a Google review of today's [job]. Mention one real detail and my link [link]. Warm, no pressure.
Reply to this 5 star review in 2 personal sentences: [paste]. Mention the detail they mentioned so it never reads like a template.
Reply in public to this 1 star review: [paste]. Stay calm, thank them, own what is fair, offer to fix it at [contact]. Under 80 words. No arguing.
Here are my last [X] reviews: [paste]. What do customers praise most, what do they complain about most, and which 3 things should I fix first?
Write a short message asking [customer] if I can quote their review on my website and socials. Make it easy to say yes or no.
Write a text asking a happy customer for a referral. Thank them, say who I help best: [ideal customer], and give one easy way to share: [link].
I will describe how I do [task]. Write it back as a step by step checklist a new hire could follow on day one. Ask me about any unclear step.
Write a job post for a [role] at my [business]: the daily work, must haves, nice to haves, pay: [range], and 3 screening questions.
Here is my to do list: [paste]. Sort it into today, this week, delegate, and drop. Be honest about what can wait.
Sort these expenses into categories in a table: [paste]. Flag anything that looks duplicated, forgotten, or off.
Turn these messy meeting notes into actions: [paste]. Who does what by when, in a table, plus every decision we made.
Draft a [policy] for my team handbook. Plain words, short, no legal speak. List what I should check with a lawyer before I use it.
